Previously, we found that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,1}\frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-3x+2}=-1.
$$

 

Applying the product rule to the original limit, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,1}\frac{(x-1)f(x)}{{x}^{2}-3x+2} & ={lim}_{x\to \,1}[\frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-3x+2}\cdot f(x)] \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \,1}\frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-3x+2}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \,1}\frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-3x+2}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \,1}5sin⁡(2x) \\  & =(-1)\cdot 5sin⁡(2\cdot 1) \\  & =-5\cdot sin⁡(2)\end{aligned}
$$
